mainTopic: Whether a thief acquires through the owner's יאוש, offhand remarks (מסיח לפי תומו) about bees and other cases, court conditions from יהושע, and recovering stolen items from a buyer.
overview: The amud first settles a question about רבי's statement that 'a גנב is like a גזלן.' Did he mean a גזלן as the רבנן see him, so the thief does not acquire, or as רבי שמעון sees him, so the thief does acquire? Two proofs, from the משנה of the customs collectors and from a ברייתא about הקדש, are pushed aside by reading the 'thief' as an armed bandit. רב אשי then proves from רבי's teaching to his son about returning stolen animals 'for their father's honor' that רבי meant רבי שמעון's view. Next the גמרא explains the משנה about a swarm of bees: the finder may keep it only if the owners gave up hope, and a woman or child is believed when speaking offhandedly. רב אשי limits offhand remarks to עדות אשה, and each challenge to this is answered by showing that the case is only rabbinic. A ברייתא teaches court conditions from the time of יהושע that let a person save his friend's property and be paid back for his loss. Finally, a new משנה about finding your stolen items with a buyer leads to a careful definition of when a report of theft is trusted. The amud ends with רבא beginning to limit that rule to an owner who usually sells his vessels, and his ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The accepted ruling: like a robber according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion: we rule that a גנב is like a גזלן according to רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that a thief is like a robber, according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier discussion by stating the accepted ruling. This is the conclusion that the coming section will explain and prove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that an owner gives up hope (יאוש) when a גזלן takes his item. So if a גנב is 'like a גזלן' by רבי שמעון's view, the owner gives up hope in a theft case too.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / the accepted ruling is
A robber, who takes openly by force

phrases.english: And we hold: like a robber, according to Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: This is the ruling on רבי's words, 'a thief is like a robber.' The גמרא explains how it reaches this in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from earlier on the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גנב is treated like a גזלן according to רבי שמעון, so the owner gives up hope and the stolen item can be acquired.

steps.title: Back to רבי's statement: a thief is like a robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to examine רבי's statement on its own: 'I say a גנב is like a גזלן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבי says: I say that a thief is like a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי's statement again so it can study it directly. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי compares a גנב to a גזלן. But he does not say whose view of a גזלן he means. The רבנן and רבי שמעון disagree about whether an owner gives up hope when a גזלן takes his item.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a quoted source directly

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi says, I say:
A thief is like a robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source behind the ruling in step 1 to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי holds that a גנב has the same law as a גזלן.

steps.title: Which view of a robber did רבי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: did רבי mean a גזלן according to the רבנן, so the thief does not acquire, or according to רבי שמעון, so the thief does acquire?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: did רבי mean 'like a robber' according to the רבנן, so the thief does not acquire? Or did he mean 'like a robber' according to רבי שמעון, so the thief does acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question about what רבי meant. It gives two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the רבנן, the owner does not give up hope when a גזלן takes his item, so a גנב who is 'like a גזלן' would not acquire. By רבי שמעון, the owner does give up hope, so the גנב would acquire. Which reading is correct decides the whole law.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
The חכמים who argue with רבי שמעון

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: by the רבנן, a גזלן is the case where the owner does NOT give up hope. By רבי שמעון, a גזלן IS the case where the owner gives up hope. The same word 'like a robber' leads to opposite results.

phrases.english: They asked:
Was he saying like a robber of the Rabbis, so he does not acquire;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כְּגַזְלָן דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר, וּקְנֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps he was saying like a robber of Rabbi Shimon, so he acquires?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exactly the statement in step 2 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי's 'like a גזלן' follows the רבנן's view (no acquisition) or רבי שמעון's view (acquisition).

steps.title: A proof from the משנה of the customs collectors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where customs collectors took someone's donkey as a possible way to answer the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if customs collectors took his donkey, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a משנה. In that משנה, items taken by customs collectors and by bandits become the new holder's, because the owners gave up hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes the owner gives up hope both in the robber case (the מוכסין) and in the thief case. This seems to show a theft case where the owner gives up hope, which could tell us how to read רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Customs or tax collectors who take things openly
The owner giving up hope of getting his item back

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If customs collectors took his donkey, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: they gave him another donkey in its place, and bandits did the same with a garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Whether owners give up hope in theft cases, which shows how to read רבי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נטלו מוכסין חמורו (customs collectors took his donkey).

steps.title: Who wrote this משנה? Neither view fits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה fits neither the רבנן, because of the robber case, nor רבי שמעון, because of the thief case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this משנה? If it is the רבנן, the robber case is a problem. If it is רבי שמעון, the thief case is a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה does not match either side of the argument. This sets up the next move, where רבי's view will explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say owners give up hope only from a גנב, so the משנה's robber case does not fit them. רבי שמעון says owners give up hope only from a גזלן, so the משנה's thief case does not fit him. The משנה must follow a third view where owners give up hope in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the author (of this source)?

steps.whyThisMatters: The only view that fits both cases is one where a גנב is like a גזלן according to רבי שמעון. That is the ruling stated in step 1.

phrases.english: Who is it?
If the Rabbis, the robber is difficult!
phrases.notes: The customs collectors count as robbers here, but the רבנן say owners do not give up hope from a robber.

phrases.english: If Rabbi Shimon, the thief is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the משנה brought in step 4 and finds that neither known view fits it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Who the author of the משנה of the customs collectors could be.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has owners give up hope from both a גזלן and a גנב. The רבנן admit this only for a גנב, and רבי שמעון only for a גזלן, so neither fits the whole משנה.

steps.title: The משנה fits רבי if he meant רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: If רבי meant a גזלן according to רבי שמעון, then a thief acquires, and the משנה can be explained as following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that רבי meant a גזלן according to רבי שמעון, so the thief acquires. Then whose view is this משנה? It is רבי's, and that is why the thief acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה of the customs collectors fits nicely if רבי meant a גזלן according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that owners give up hope (יאוש) when a גזלן takes their things. רבי adds that a גנב is treated the same way. So both cases in the משנה, the robber case and the thief case, would end with the taker acquiring, and the משנה matches רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say… (the first half of a 'this side works, that side doesn't' proof)
He acquires (the stolen item becomes his)
The owner giving up hope of getting his item back

phrases.english: Granted, if you say that רבי
was saying 'like a robber' according to רבי שמעון,
and so the thief acquires;
whose view is this משנה? It is רבי's,
and that is why the thief acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the problem raised in step 5 (the משנה fits neither the רבנן nor רבי שמעון) to show that only one reading of רבי rescues it.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי meant a גזלן according to רבי שמעון, so a thief acquires.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the customs collectors and the ליסטים, where in both cases the owner is assumed to give up hope.

steps.title: The other reading leaves the משנה with no author
steps.stepSummary: If רבי meant a גזלן according to the רבנן, the thief does not acquire, and the משנה would match nobody.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that רבי meant a גזלן according to the רבנן, so the thief does not acquire, then whose view is this משנה? It is not רבי, not רבי שמעון, and not the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by showing that the other reading of רבי leaves the משנה without any תנא who could have said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, רבי holds that neither a גנב nor a גזלן acquires. The רבנן let only a גנב acquire, and רבי שמעון lets only a גזלן acquire. The משנה lets both acquire, so it would match nobody, which seems to prove that רבי meant a גזלן according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say… (the second half of the proof, the side that fails)

keyTerms.term: לָא רַבִּי וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְלָא רַבָּנַן
keyTerms.meaning: Not רבי, not רבי שמעון, and not the רבנן: no one could be the author

steps.whatToRemember: The proof seems to show that רבי meant a גזלן as רבי שמעון views him, so a גנב acquires. The next steps reject this proof.

phrases.english: But if you say
that he was saying 'like a robber' according to the רבנן,
so the thief does not acquire;
then whose view is this משנה?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְלָא רַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: It is not רבי, not רבי שמעון, and not the רבנן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided proof begun in step 6 by showing that the other option fails.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי could not have meant a גזלן according to the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the customs collectors, which no תנא could have authored under this reading.

steps.title: The משנה is about an armed bandit, following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ליסטים in the משנה is an armed bandit, who counts as a גזלן, so the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? An armed bandit, and the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the משנה's ליסטים case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the ליסטים in the משנה was a thief, a גנב. If he is an armed bandit who takes things openly by force, he is really a גזלן. רבי שמעון already holds that owners give up hope with a גזלן, so the משנה fits רבי שמעון, and it teaches us nothing about what רבי meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
An armed bandit, who takes by force

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying a ליסטים is never a thief. It only says the ליסטים in this משנה can be read as an armed bandit, which makes him a גזלן.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With an armed bandit,
and the משנה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 6 and 7 by redefining the ליסטים case in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה about what רבי meant.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ליסטים was a thief, but he can be an armed bandit, who is a גזלן. That lets the משנה fit רבי שמעון without involving רבי.

steps.title: Then the bandit case is just the robber case again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the ליסטים is a גזלן, he is the same as the customs collector case, so why does the משנה repeat itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as a גזלן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 8, saying it makes the משנה repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The customs collector case in the משנה is already a case of a גזלן. If the ליסטים case is also a גזלן, the משנה would be teaching the same law twice, and a משנה does not normally repeat itself for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introducing a problem with the last answer)

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as a robber!
phrases.notes: The 'robber' here is the משנה's first case, the customs collector who took a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the armed-bandit answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ליסטים in the משנה is an armed bandit (a גזלן).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both cases in the משנה are a גזלן, the second case adds nothing, which makes the משנה repetitive.

steps.title: Two different kinds of robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching two different kinds of גזלן: the customs collector and the armed bandit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of גזלן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the armed-bandit reading by explaining why the משנה lists both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The customs collector and the armed bandit both take by force, but in different ways, so the משנה teaches that the owner gives up hope in each of them. With that, the משנה stands as following רבי שמעון, and the proof about what רבי meant is gone.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the customs collector משנה fails: it can follow רבי שמעון by treating the ליסטים as an armed גזלן. A proof that holds comes in steps 17-19.

phrases.english: It teaches two types of robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition problem of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the apparent repetition as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases in the משנה are the same kind of גזלן, so one of them is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two different kinds of גזלן, so both cases are needed.

steps.title: A new proof from the ברייתא about consecrated items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof: a ברייתא says that a גנב, a גזלן, and an אנס can make stolen items הקדש, תרומה, and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a thief, a robber, and one who forces a sale. Their הקדש is הקדש, their תרומה is תרומה, and their מעשר is מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try again to answer the question of what רבי meant. This step only quotes the ברייתא and sets up the argument, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only make something הקדש, תרומה, or מעשר if it belongs to him. Since the ברייתא says these take effect for both a גנב and a גזלן, it seems to show that both acquire the stolen item. The גמרא will work out who the author is in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who forces another to sell him something
Something dedicated to the בית המקדש
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a thief, a robber, and one who forces a sale —
their consecrated items are consecrated,
and their תרומה is תרומה,
and their tithes are tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא returns to the question of step 3 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: What רבי meant in saying a גנב is like a גזלן: whether the thief acquires.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that a גנב, a גזלן, and an אנס can make stolen items הקדש, תרומה, and מעשר.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא? Each side has a problem
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lets both a גנב and a גזלן make stolen items holy. The רבנן cannot explain the robber case, and רבי שמעון cannot explain the thief case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is the רבנן, the robber case is difficult. If it is רבי שמעון, the thief case is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who could have taught the ברייתא from step 11. It shows that neither the רבנן nor רבי שמעון fits it neatly. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only make something הקדש if it is his, and a stolen item becomes his only after the owner gives up hope (יאוש). The רבנן hold that a robbery victim does not give up hope, so the robber case is a problem for them. רבי שמעון holds that a theft victim does not give up hope, so the thief case is a problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Who is the author?
The owner giving up hope of getting his item back
Making an item holy, dedicated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Whose view is it? If it is the Rabbis, the robber is difficult;
phrases.notes: For the רבנן, a robbery victim never gives up hope, so how could the robber make the item holy?

phrases.english: if it is Rabbi Shimon, the thief is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in step 11 to find its author.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא to either the רבנן or רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes the owner gives up hope in both the thief and robber cases. Each of the two known views denies hope-giving-up in one of those cases.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits only if רבי meant רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: If רבי said a thief is like a robber according to רבי שמעון, the ברייתא fits רבי. If he meant the רבנן's robber, the ברייתא fits nobody.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say רבי meant a thief is like a robber according to רבי שמעון. That is why the thief acquires the item. But if you say he meant a thief is like a robber according to the רבנן, then whose view is this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. Only one reading of רבי gives the ברייתא an author, so that reading must be correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a robbery victim gives up hope. If רבי extends that to a thief, then in both cases the owner gives up hope, and the ברייתא matches רבי exactly. If רבי meant the רבנן's robber, where the owner does not give up hope, the ברייתא would match no one at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say... (opens a 'this reading works, that one doesn't' argument)
A thief is like a robber (רבי's rule)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that he was saying a thief is like a robber according to Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי, whose rule 'a thief is like a robber' this whole discussion is about.

phrases.english: that is why he acquires;
but if you say
a thief is like a robber according to the Rabbis,
then whose view is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא גַּנָּב כְּגַזְלָן דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the problem from step 12 to prove how רבי's rule should be read.
steps.raayaObject: רבי meant that a thief is like a robber according to רבי שמעון (the owner gives up hope).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a גנב, a גזלן and an אנס can make stolen items הקדש, תרומה and מעשר.

steps.title: The 'thief' is really an armed bandit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The thief in the ברייתא is an armed bandit, who counts as a robber, so the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about an armed bandit, and the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof the same way it did in step 8. The ברייתא can follow רבי שמעון after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'גנב' in the ברייתא is an armed bandit, then legally he is a גזלן. רבי שמעון holds that a robbery victim gives up hope, so both cases fit רבי שמעון. Now the ברייתא does not need רבי, and the proof about how to read רבי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: An armed bandit, who takes things openly by force

phrases.english: It is about an armed bandit,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 13 by redefining the ברייתא's thief.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof entirely, since the ברייתא can now follow רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the 'גנב' is an ordinary sneak thief, but he may be an armed bandit.

steps.title: Then the thief is the same as the robber
steps.stepSummary: If the 'thief' is an armed bandit, he is just a robber, so why does the ברייתא list him separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he is the same as the robber!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection. The ברייתא already listed a robber, so calling the thief a robber makes the list repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not normally list the same case twice. If the armed bandit is legally a גזלן, then 'גנב' and 'גזלן' in the list would mean the same thing.

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as a robber!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's thief is an armed bandit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bandit is a גזלן, the ברייתא repeats the robber case for no reason.

steps.title: Two kinds of robber
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists two different kinds of robber: the ordinary robber and the armed bandit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the list does not repeat itself. It teaches two different types of גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are legally robbers, but they are different real-life cases, so the ברייתא names each one. This matches the answer in step 10. The proof about how to read רבי stays rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about making stolen items holy cannot prove how to read רבי's rule. Its 'thief' may be an armed bandit, which is a second kind of robber, and then it follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Two kinds of robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one category into two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing the armed bandit next to the robber looks like a repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches two separate kinds of גזלן, so nothing is repeated.

steps.title: רב אשי brings רבי's teaching to his son
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי opens a new proof. רבי taught his son that heirs must return even a well-known cow or donkey that their father stole, because of their father's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רבה: Come and hear what רבי taught his son רבי שמעון. The rule is not only about things that actually serve as a guarantee for a loan. Even a cow he plows with, or a donkey he walks behind, the heirs must return, out of honor for their father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new proof about how to understand רבי, using רבי's own explanation of a משנה. This step quotes the source; the reasoning from it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said heirs of a robber must return the stolen item if it is something that can back a loan, like land. רבי widens this to well-known animals, like a cow the father plowed with in public. He says the reason is to protect their father's honor, not that the item still strictly belongs to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that backs a loan, mainly land
Driving a donkey by walking behind it

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי שמעון here is רבי's son, the student hearing the lesson. He is not the תנא רבי שמעון whose view was discussed until now.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rabba:
Come and hear,
that Rabbi taught Rabbi Shimon his son:
phrases.notes: He is explaining the משנה on דף קיא about children who inherit something their father stole.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת מַמָּשׁ;
phrases.english: not only something that actually serves as a guarantee;
rather, even a cow that he plows with,
or a donkey that he drives from behind,
they are obligated to return,
because of the honor of their father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַבָּה תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous proof was rejected, a new proof is brought from a different source.
steps.raayaObject: How to read רבי's rule that a thief is like a robber (the reasoning follows in the next lines).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's teaching to his son רבי שמעון about heirs returning stolen animals out of honor for their father.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof now comes from רבי's own words, so it may show directly how he himself understood stolen property.

steps.title: The father's honor shows which robber רבי meant
steps.stepSummary: Because the heirs must return the animal only for their father's honor, the גמרא concludes that רבי was talking about the robber of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason the heirs must return it is their father's honor. Without that, they would not have to return it. So we learn that when רבי said a thief is like a robber, he meant the robber of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב אשי's proof by reading closely the words 'because of their father's honor.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only reason to return the animal is the father's honor, then by the basic law the heirs could keep it, which means the owner had given up hope and the item no longer belongs to him. The רבנן hold that an owner does not give up hope from a robber, while רבי שמעון holds that he does. So רבי's comparison of a thief to a robber must use רבי שמעון's robber.

keyTerms.meaning: But if not for this, then no (reading the opposite case out of a statement)
The robber as רבי שמעון rules about him

steps.whyThisMatters: It settles the question asked in step 3, which the two earlier proofs (steps 4-10 and 11-16) failed to answer, about which opinion רבי's statement follows.

phrases.english: The reason is because of their father's honor,
phrases.notes: This goes back to what רבי taught his son in step 17: the heirs return the well-known cow or donkey.

phrases.english: but if not for their father's honor, they would not have to;
learn from it: רבי
was speaking about the robber of רבי שמעון!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד אֲבִיהֶן, הָא לָאו כְּבוֹד אֲבִיהֶן – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that רב אשי began in step 17 by drawing the inference.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי's 'a thief is like a robber' refers to רבי שמעון's robber
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's instruction to his son that heirs return the well-known animal only because of their father's honor

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: yes, learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof, and this question is closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time no one rejects the proof, unlike in step 14. So the conclusion stands: רבי compared a thief to the robber of רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; when said alone as an answer, it means 'indeed, so it is'
Robber (one who takes openly, by force)

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: when רבי said a thief is like a robber, he meant the robber as רבי שמעון rules about him.
steps.confusionAlert: 'שמע מינה' shows up twice in a row. The first time is the proof's claim. The second time is the גמרא agreeing with it.

phrases.english: Learn from it, indeed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference made in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי's comparison of a thief to a robber follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'and so too' about bees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about a swarm of bees and asks what the word 'וכן' is adding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And so too a swarm of bees.' What does 'and so too' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה, and asks why bees are added with the word 'וכן.' This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already taught that if the owners gave up hope, the finder may keep the items. The גמרא wants to know what new point bees add to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too, meaning the same rule applies

phrases.english: "And so too a swarm of bees."
What is "and so too"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the thief-and-robber discussion and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the משנה teaches by adding bees with 'וכן'

steps.title: Bees need real giving up of hope too
steps.stepSummary: Bees are owned only through a קנין דרבנן, so one might think the owner surely gives up hope. The משנה teaches that the finder may keep them only if we know the owners gave up hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: even a swarm of bees, which a person owns only by a rabbinic kind of ownership, follows the same rule. You might have thought that since only the rabbis made it his, the owner surely gives up hope even when we know nothing. So the משנה teaches: if the owners gave up hope, yes, the finder keeps it. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'וכן' tells us bees are no exception: the finder may keep them only when the owners actually gave up hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ownership of bees is only rabbinic, we might assume the owner takes it lightly and gives up hope right away, even without saying so. The משנה rejects that idea. Even here we need a clear יאוש, just as with any other lost item.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying
Ownership that comes only from rabbinic law
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
An unclear case, where we don't know what the owner thinks
Giving up hope of getting something back

steps.whatToRemember: Even for bees, which are owned only through a קנין דרבנן, the finder keeps them only if we know the owners gave up hope.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
even a swarm of bees,
which is owned only by rabbinic acquisition.
It might have entered your mind to say:
this one, since it is merely the rabbis
who make it his,
even in an unclear case he also gives up hope;
so it teaches us:
if the owners gave up hope, yes,
if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נְחִיל שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word 'וכן' asked in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וכן' teaches that even for bees, which are owned only through a קנין דרבנן, the finder keeps them only if the owners actually gave up hope. We do not assume they did.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה on a woman and a child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says a woman and a minor are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה said: A woman and a minor are believed, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to start a new discussion. This line sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a woman or a child is believed to say that the swarm came out of a certain person's hive, and so it belongs to him. This is surprising, because they are usually not accepted as witnesses. The גמרא is about to discuss why.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה said:
A woman and a minor are believed, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: they are believed to say, 'This swarm came out from here.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה: נֶאֱמֶנֶת אִשָּׁה וְקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after finishing the 'וכן' discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman or a minor is believed to identify where a swarm of bees came from.

steps.title: Can a woman and a minor be witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: a woman and a minor are not valid witnesses, so how can they be believed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are a woman and a minor fit to give testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the line it just quoted from the משנה. Women and minors normally cannot testify, so why are they believed here?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that women and minors are not accepted as witnesses. Yet רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה said they are believed about the bees. The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge to his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are fit to give testimony
A woman and a minor (a child)

phrases.english: A woman and a minor
are they fit for testimony?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's ruling that a woman and a minor are believed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women and minors are not valid witnesses, so their word should count for nothing.

steps.title: They spoke offhandedly while the owners chased the bees
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the case is one where the owners were chasing the swarm, and the woman or child casually said where it came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: We are dealing with a case where the owners were chasing after the bees. A woman or a minor was speaking innocently and said, "This swarm came out from here."
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge. The woman and child are not giving formal testimony in court. They are just speaking casually while the owners chase the bees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer narrows the case. Their words are believed because they spoke offhandedly, without knowing it mattered, while the owners were visibly chasing the swarm. This is not formal עדות, so the rule that women and minors cannot testify does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrowed case)
Speaking innocently and offhandedly, without meaning to testify

steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of מסיח לפי תומו, which drives the rest of the discussion.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where the owners were chasing after them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the bees.

phrases.english: and a woman and a minor were speaking innocently,
and saying: From here this swarm came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman and minor seem to be serving as formal witnesses, which they cannot do.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are only speaking offhandedly while the owners chase the bees, and such casual words are believed here.

steps.title: Offhand remarks count only for a woman's testimony
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that an offhand remark is accepted only for testimony that frees a woman to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: An offhand speaker is accepted only for testimony about a woman, and nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic of offhand speech came up, רב אשי gives a general rule about it. It is accepted only in one area: testimony that a woman's husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony that a husband died lets his wife remarry. In that area the חכמים were lenient and accepted offhand remarks. רב אשי says this is the only place such remarks are accepted, which sets up the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that a woman's husband died, so she may remarry

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
One who speaks offhandedly is not valid
except for testimony about a woman alone.
phrases.notes: He means testimony that her husband died, so she can remarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the idea of offhand speech from step 24 and gives a general rule about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offhand remarks are accepted only for עדות אשה.

steps.title: But the bees case accepts offhand remarks
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי: the swarm of bees is a case of offhand speech that is accepted, and it has nothing to do with a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: And is it not accepted elsewhere? But the swarm of bees is a case of someone speaking offhandedly!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's rule. The משנה about the bees accepts offhand speech in a money matter, not a woman's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said offhand remarks count only for עדות אשה. The bees case, as שמואל just explained it, shows them counting in a different area. So the rule seems too narrow.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
And not?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really never accepted anywhere else?

phrases.english: But look at the swarm of bees:
it is a case of one speaking offhandedly!
phrases.notes: This is how שמואל explained the משנה in step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's rule (step 25) using שמואל's explanation (step 24).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that offhand speech is accepted only for עדות אשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bees case accepts offhand speech in a matter that is not about a woman.

steps.title: Bees are different because ownership is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: Bees are owned only through a rabbinic acquisition, so the חכמים could be lenient and accept offhand remarks.
steps.simpleTranslation: A swarm of bees is different, because owning it is only a rabbinic form of acquisition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's rule is defended. The bees are an exception because owning them is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ownership of bees comes only from the חכמים, they had the power to accept weaker evidence about it, like offhand speech. This does not break רב אשי's rule for matters that come from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownership that comes only from the Rabbis, not from the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Bees are still real property. The point is only that the owner's claim on them is rabbinic, so the rules of evidence can be more lenient.

phrases.english: A swarm of bees is different,
since it is a rabbinic acquisition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): a rabbinic matter allows leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bees case shows offhand speech is accepted generally.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is accepted there only because ownership of bees is rabbinic.

steps.title: A Torah-level case accepting an offhand remark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether offhand speech is never accepted on a Torah-level matter. It brings שמואל's story of a man who casually remembered being immersed as a child to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on a Torah-level matter, is it not accepted? But רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: There was a man who was speaking offhandedly and said, "I remember when I was a child, riding on my father's shoulder. They took me out of school, took off my shirt, and immersed me so I could eat תרומה in the evening."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that offhand speech works only for rabbinic matters or for a woman's case. It starts a story about a man's casual memory from childhood, which the גמרא is about to use as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating תרומה is for כהנים only, so the man's memory hints that his family were כהנים. That is a Torah-level matter. If his casual words are relied on there, offhand speech counts beyond עדות אשה and rabbinic cases. The next step finishes the story.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly portion of produce, eaten only by כהנים

phrases.english: And on a Torah matter, not?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel said:
There was an incident with a certain man
who was speaking offhandedly, and said:
"I remember when I was a small child,
and I was riding on Father's shoulder,
and they took me out of school,
and they took off my shirt,
and they immersed me to eat תרומה in the evening."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in steps 25 and 27, that offhand speech works only for עדות אשה or rabbinic matters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that offhand speech is not accepted for Torah-level matters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man's offhand childhood memory seems to be relied on for a Torah-level issue, eating תרומה as a כהן.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל

steps.title: רבי חנינא's ending: the man was raised to the priesthood
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא adds the end of the story: the man's friends called him 'יוחנן who eats חלות', and רבי raised him to כהונה based on his casual remark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא finishes the story this way: the man said, 'My friends would keep away from me and call me יוחנן the eater of חלות.' And רבי raised him to כהונה because of what he said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story that started the challenge in step 28. The ending shows that רבי actually relied on the man's casual remark to treat him as a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story only becomes a real challenge once we hear that רבי acted on it. Eating תרומה or חלה is forbidden to a non-כהן, so letting someone eat it because of an offhand remark seems to show that such remarks are trusted even on a Torah-level matter. That contradicts רב אשי, who said they are trusted only to let a woman remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן; only כהנים may eat it, like תרומה
They kept themselves apart from me
He raised him to the priesthood, meaning he gave him the full status of a כהן

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina finishes it like this:
"And my friends would keep apart from me,
and they would call me:
'Yochanan, eater of חלות.'"
phrases.notes: His friends knew he ate the כהן's dough portion, so they treated him as a כהן.

phrases.english: And רבי raised him to the priesthood based on his word!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun in step 28 and makes the challenge fully explicit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule (step 25) that an offhand remark is accepted only for letting a woman remarry.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי relied on a casual remark to let a man eat תרומה and חלה, which are forbidden to non-כהנים. That suggests casual remarks are trusted even on a Torah-level matter.

steps.title: It was only rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The case involved only תרומה דרבנן, so the חכמים could be lenient and accept the casual remark.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was about תרומה that is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי only let the man eat תרומה that is a rabbinic obligation, not a Torah one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as step 27. On a rabbinic matter the חכמים can choose to accept a casual remark. So the story does not prove that casual remarks are trusted on Torah-level matters, and רב אשי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה that is obligatory only by rabbinic law, not by the Torah

phrases.english: With תרומה that is only rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 28-29 by limiting the case to a rabbinic level.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ruling concerned only a rabbinic matter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי relied on a casual remark for a Torah-level prohibition of תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תרומה was only rabbinic, so the leniency does not apply to Torah-level matters.

steps.title: The captive child who watched over his mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a child casually said he always kept his mind on his mother while they were captives, and רבי let her marry a כהן based on his word. That is a Torah-level matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, is a casual remark never trusted on a Torah matter? When רב דימי came, he reported that רב חנא of Carthage (some say רב אחא of Carthage) told this story: A case came before רבי יהושע בן לוי (some say before רבי) about a child who was speaking casually and said, 'My mother and I were captured among the gentiles. When I went out to draw water, my mind was on my mother. When I went to gather wood, my mind was on my mother.' And רבי married her off to a כהן based on his word!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again whether a casual remark is really never trusted on a Torah-level matter. It brings a new story that seems to show it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman held captive by gentiles is suspected of having been violated, and the challenger assumes this would forbid her to a כהן by Torah law. The child's casual words showed that he watched her the whole time, and רבי relied on them to let her marry a כהן. The case is not about letting a woman remarry after her husband's death, so it seems to contradict רב אשי. The next step answers that this ban is really rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: And still, meaning: even so, is that really true?
Speaking casually and innocently, without meaning to testify

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a case of freeing a woman whose husband died. The child's words are about whether a captive woman stayed pure enough to marry a כהן, so רב אשי's exception for a woman remarrying does not cover it.

phrases.english: And still, is it really never accepted on a Torah matter?
But when רב דימי came,
he said that רב חנא of Carthage,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַחָא קַרְטִיגָנָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי:
phrases.english: and some say רב אחא of Carthage, told this story:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: A case came before רבי יהושע בן לוי,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי,
phrases.english: and some say the case came before רבי,
about a certain child
who was speaking casually, and said:
"My mother and I were taken captive among the gentiles.

phrases.aramaic: יָצָאתִי לִשְׁאוֹב מַיִם – דַּעְתִּי עַל אִמִּי,
phrases.english: When I went out to draw water, my mind was on my mother;
when I went to gather wood, my mind was on my mother."
And רבי married her off to a כהן based on his word!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rabbinic-תרומה answer in step 30, brings a new case that seems to involve a Torah-level prohibition.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule (step 25), together with the answer in step 30 that the casual remark was accepted only on a rabbinic matter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying a former captive to a כהן involves a Torah-level prohibition, and the case is not about letting a woman remarry after her husband's death. Yet רבי relied on the child's casual remark, so casual remarks seem to be trusted on Torah-level matters too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage of the sugya, which must explain why the casual remark was trusted in a captive woman's case.

steps.title: The captive woman case was only a rabbinic stringency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that for a שבויה the חכמים were lenient, because her ban from a כהן is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a captive woman, the חכמים were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the child who spoke about his mother in captivity. That case was not really a Torah-level matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a woman taken captive may still marry a כהן. Only the חכמים forbade her, out of worry that she was harmed. Since the ban is rabbinic, the חכמים could accept a child's offhand remark, just as with the bees and with תרומה דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was taken captive
Someone speaking offhandedly, without meaning to testify

steps.whatToRemember: All three challenges (the bees, the man who ate תרומה, the captive woman) are answered the same way: the matter is only rabbinic. So רב אשי's rule stands: on Torah-level matters, offhand speech is trusted only for letting a woman remarry.

phrases.english: With a captive woman they were lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31 about the child's remark regarding his captive mother.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the case as rabbinic, not Torah-level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The captive woman case seemed to be a Torah-level matter where an offhand remark was accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her ban is only rabbinic, so offhand speech can be relied on there.

steps.title: A court condition lets one cut a friend's branch to save his bees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that one may not cut another's branch. It then brings a ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who says a court condition allows cutting the branch, with payment for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But he may not cut his branch.' A ברייתא teaches that רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: It is a condition of the court that a person may go down into his friend's field and cut his friend's branch to save his own swarm. He then pays for the branch out of his swarm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about bees that settled on someone else's branch. It brings a ברייתא with a different view: the bee owner may cut the branch and then pay for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the bee owner may not cut the branch, even if he will pay. רבי ישמעאל says the court set up a standing condition that does allow it. The branch owner is not left with a loss, because he is paid the branch's value from the bees.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition set by the court that binds everyone automatically

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the bee owner gets the branch for free. The ברייתא says the branch owner is paid its value out of the swarm.

phrases.english: But he may not cut his branch, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. The bees settled on a branch belonging to someone else.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
It is a condition of the court,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא יוֹרֵד לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֶה שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: that he may go down into his friend's field

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹצֵץ סוֹכוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, לְהַצִּיל אֶת נְחִילוֹ.
phrases.english: and cut his friend's branch, to save his swarm.

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹטֵל דְּמֵי סוֹכוֹ מִתּוֹךְ נְחִילוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: And he takes the value of his branch from his friend's swarm.
phrases.notes: Now 'he' is the field owner. He gets paid for his branch out of the bee owner's swarm.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the offhand-remarks discussion and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under a court condition, one may cut a friend's branch to save his own bees, paying the branch's value from the swarm.

steps.title: More court conditions: wine for honey, wood for flax, set up by יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds two more court conditions. One may pour out his wine to save a friend's honey, or unload his wood to carry a friend's flax, and be paid back from the saved goods. These conditions go back to when יהושע divided the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also a condition of the court that a person may pour out his wine to save his friend's honey, and take the value of his wine from his friend's honey. It is also a condition of the court that he may unload his wood and load his friend's flax, and take the value of his wood from his friend's flax. For on this condition יהושע gave the land to ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with two more cases built the same way. It then gives the reason all of them work: they were conditions set when יהושע divided ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case a person gives up something cheaper (wine, wood) to save his friend's more valuable goods (honey, flax). He does not lose out, because he is paid from what he saved. The rule binds everyone because the land was handed out on this condition from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave as an inheritance or portion

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of conditions tied to how יהושע divided the land. They create a lasting duty to save another person's property, while making sure the person who helps is paid back.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַאי בֵּית דִּין הוּא, שֶׁיְּהֵא שׁוֹפֵךְ יֵינוֹ
phrases.english: And it is a condition of the court that he may pour out his wine
and save his friend's honey,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹטֵל דְּמֵי יֵינוֹ מִתּוֹךְ דּוּבְשָׁנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and take the value of his wine from his friend's honey.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַאי בֵּית דִּין הוּא, שֶׁיְּהֵא מְפָרֵק אֶת עֵצָיו
phrases.english: And it is a condition of the court that he may unload his wood
and load his friend's flax,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹטֵל דְּמֵי עֵצָיו מִתּוֹךְ פִּשְׁתָּנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and take the value of his wood from his friend's flax.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן הִנְחִיל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: For on this condition Yehoshua gave the land to Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַאי בֵּית דִּין הוּא, שֶׁיְּהֵא שׁוֹפֵךְ יֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with two more court conditions and the reason behind all of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may give up cheaper goods to save a friend's costlier goods and be paid back from them, by a condition going back to יהושע.

steps.title: New משנה: recognizing your stolen items in someone else's hands
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If a person recognizes his vessels and books in someone else's hands, and it is known in town that he was robbed, the buyer swears how much he paid, gets that money back, and returns the items. If there was no such rumor, the owner cannot claim them, since he may simply have sold them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone recognizes his vessels and books in another person's hands, and word spread in the city that he had been robbed. The buyer swears to him how much he paid, and takes that amount. If not, he has no power to claim them, because I can say: he sold them to someone else, and this person bought them from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It deals with a person who finds items he says were stolen from him in the hands of someone who bought them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is known in town that a theft happened, the owner's claim is believable. He gets the items back, but he must pay the buyer the price the buyer swears he paid. Without such a rumor, we assume the owner may have sold the items himself, so he has no claim.

keyTerms.meaning: A public report that a theft happened
The buyer, who now holds the items

steps.confusionAlert: The one who swears is the buyer, not the original owner. He swears how much he paid so he can get that money back.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who recognizes his vessels and his books in another's hand,
and word went out in the city that he was robbed –

phrases.aramaic: יִשָּׁבַע לוֹ לוֹקֵחַ כַּמָּה נָתַן, וְיִטּוֹל.
phrases.english: the buyer swears to him how much he paid, and takes it.
And if not – it is not in his power,
phrases.notes: 'If not' means there was no rumor of a theft. Then the owner cannot demand the items.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָן לְאַחֵר, וּלְקָחָן זֶה הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: for I say: he sold them to another, and this one bought them from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the court-condition discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a public report of theft, the owner takes back his items after paying the buyer the price he swears to. Without it, the owner has no claim.

steps.title: Why should a rumor of theft be trusted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a rumor of theft in town should help the owner. Maybe he sold the items and then spread the rumor himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if a rumor of theft spread about him in the city, what of it? Let us worry that maybe he sold them, and he himself is the one spreading the rumor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by challenging it. Why does a rumor of theft prove anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the town rumor as strong enough to take the items away from the buyer. But a rumor can be faked. The owner may have sold his things, regretted it, and then told people they were stolen so he could get them back cheaply.

keyTerms.meaning: A reputation or rumor that a theft happened
Let us be concerned, let us worry
Spreads the rumor, literally 'puts out the name'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a theft never helps the owner. It is asking only what kind of rumor is strong enough to trust.

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי יָצָא לוֹ שֵׁם גְּנֵיבָה בָּעִיר –
phrases.english: And if a rumor of theft spread about him in the city,
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה from step 35.

phrases.english: what of it?
Let us worry that perhaps he sold them,
and he himself is the one spreading the rumor!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יָצָא לוֹ שֵׁם גְּנֵיבָה בָּעִיר מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of the משנה quoted in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reliance on a town rumor of theft.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rumor can be started by the owner himself after a real sale, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: Guests came and the owner shouted at night
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says the משנה means a case where guests came into the house, and at night the owner shouted that his vessels were stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: For example, people came into his house, and he got up and cried out at night and said, 'My vessels were stolen!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by describing the kind of rumor the משנה means. It is an outcry made right when strangers were in the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the rumor did not come from nowhere. Strangers were really in the house, and the owner cried out at night, right away. That timing makes the theft claim seem believable.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as a case where

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּאוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: For example, where people came into his house,
and he got up and cried out at night,
and said: My vessels were stolen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּאוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rumor in town counts, so the owner could fake it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rumor counts when guests were present and the owner cried out at night.

steps.title: That just gives him a better excuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב יהודה's case. Guests in the house only give the owner a handy excuse to claim a fake theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the more so! He found an excuse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יהודה's answer. His case does not remove the worry; it makes the worry stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shouting at night is only the owner's own word. If he sold his things and wants them back, guests in his house are the perfect cover story. So his outcry proves nothing.

phrases.english: All the more so, he has found an excuse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 37.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יהודה's case as proof of theft.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The outcry is only the owner's own claim, and the guests give him a convenient excuse to lie.

steps.title: A tunnel, guests leaving with bundles, and everyone talking
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא in the name of רב gives a stronger case: a tunnel was dug into the house, the guests were seen leaving with bundles of vessels on their shoulders, and everyone says the man was robbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא finished the statement in the name of רב: For example, there was a tunnel dug into his house, and the people who slept in his house went out with bundles of vessels on their shoulders, and everyone says, 'So-and-so's vessels were stolen.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a fuller version of רב's case. Here the proof does not depend on the owner's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is real, outside evidence. There is a dug tunnel, people saw the guests carrying bundles out, and the whole town is saying it. The owner did not make this up, so the theft is believable.

keyTerms.meaning: Finishes the statement, adds the ending
A tunnel or break-in dug into a house

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that the rumor in the משנה must rest on visible evidence that others see, not only on the owner's own claim.

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana finished it in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה מַחְתֶּרֶת חֲתוּרָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: For example, where a tunnel was dug into his house,
and the people who slept overnight in his house

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ, וְאַנְבּוּרְקְרָאוֹת שֶׁל כֵּלִים עַל כִּתְפֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: went out with bundles of vessels on their shoulders,
and everyone says: 'So-and-so's vessels were stolen.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stronger answer to step 36, avoiding the problem raised in step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case with outside evidence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner's own outcry is enough, but that was rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tunnel, guests seen with bundles, and public talk make the theft believable.

steps.title: Maybe only vessels were taken, not books
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the guests took only vessels and not books, so why must the buyer give back the books too?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe there were vessels, and there were no books!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's case. People saw bundles of vessels, but the משנה also talks about books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The evidence in step 39 shows only that vessels were stolen. The משנה also lets the owner take back books. Nothing proves books were stolen, so the owner may have really sold those.

phrases.english: But perhaps there were vessels,
and there were no books!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא כֵּלִים הֲווֹ סְפָרִים לָא הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case given in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's case as an explanation of the משנה's mention of books.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The evidence shows only that vessels were stolen, but the משנה also returns books to the owner.

steps.title: People are also saying books were stolen
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן answers that the case is where people are also saying books were stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: For example, where they are also saying 'books.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about books. The public talk includes books too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talk in town now covers both vessels and books. So the evidence supports the owner's claim on both kinds of items, and the buyer must return both, after being paid back what he spent.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'rumor of theft' is not just any talk. It means clear outside signs of a break-in plus public talk, and the talk must cover each kind of item the owner wants back, vessels and books.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
For example, where they are also saying books.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּגוֹן דְּקָאָמְרִי נָמֵי סְפָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only vessels were seen, so the books might have been sold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The public talk also says books were stolen, so both are returned.

steps.title: Maybe small books were stolen but he claims big ones
steps.stepSummary: Even if everyone agrees books were stolen, maybe only small books were taken and the owner is claiming large, expensive ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry: maybe small books were stolen, and he is claiming big ones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new worry about רבי חייא בר אבא's answer. Knowing that books were stolen does not tell us which books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 41 showed that books were stolen, but not their size or value. The owner might point to a large, valuable book in the buyer's hands and say it is his, when really only a small one was taken from him. So the challenge is about which books, not whether books were stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us worry / let us take into account

phrases.english: But let us worry: perhaps small ones were taken,
and he is claiming big ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא זוּטְרֵי, וְקָא טָעֵין רַבְרְבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 41 as not specific enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר אבא's case, where people say books were stolen (step 41).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rumor that books were stolen does not prove that these particular large books are the ones taken; the owner could be overclaiming.

steps.title: People name the exact books that were stolen
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the case is where people are saying exactly which books were stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: the case is where people are saying, 'Such-and-such a book and such-and-such a book were stolen.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the worry by making the case more specific: the talk in town names the exact books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people identify the specific books, there is no room to switch a small book for a large one. The worry about size disappears because the stolen items are known by name.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
It is where people are saying: such-and-such a book and such-and-such a book were stolen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא, דְּקָאָמְרִי: סֵפֶר פְּלוֹנִי וּפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 42.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to one where the specific books are known.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the owner is swapping a small stolen book for a large one he sees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rumor names the specific books, so there is no doubt about which ones were stolen.

steps.title: Maybe old books were stolen but he claims new ones
steps.stepSummary: Even if the titles are known, maybe old copies were stolen and he is claiming new copies of the same books.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the stolen books were old, and he is claiming new ones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Knowing the name of the book does not tell us whether the stolen copy was old or new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two copies of the same book can be worth very different amounts. The owner might be claiming a new copy he sees in the buyer's hands, when his stolen copy was old and worn.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were old,
and he is claiming new ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הֲווֹ עַתִּיקֵי, וְקָא טָעֵין חַדְתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 43: naming the book is still not specific enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's case, where people name the stolen books.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A title identifies the book but not the copy; an old copy and a new copy of the same book differ in value.

steps.title: People point to the actual items and say whose they are
steps.stepSummary: רב says the case is where people say, 'These are so-and-so's vessels, these are so-and-so's books,' identifying the exact items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the case is where people say, 'These are so-and-so's vessels, these are so-and-so's books.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers by making the case as specific as possible: people point to the very items and say they belong to this owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no question of size, age or value, because these exact objects are known to be his. This closes the series of 'maybe he is exaggerating' challenges that began in step 40.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / such as the case where

steps.whatToRemember: By the end, the משנה's case is one where people know exactly which items were stolen. Only then does the owner take back his vessels and books.

phrases.english: Rav said: for example, where people say:
"These are so-and-so's vessels,

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner might be claiming newer copies than the ones that were stolen.
steps.terutzMaskana: People recognize these very items as his, so there is no room to overclaim.

steps.title: רב also said a burglar keeps what he took
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from his own ruling: a burglar who took vessels is exempt because he 'bought them with his blood.' So how can רב say the owner takes the items back here?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say this? Didn't רב say: one who broke in through a tunnel, took vessels and left, is exempt? Why? Because he acquired them with his blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an apparent contradiction between two rulings of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A burglar (בא במחתרת) may be killed by the homeowner, so רב rules that he acquires the stolen items and is exempt from returning them. In our case there was also a tunnel (step 39), so it seems the thieves should own the items, and the owner should not be able to take them back from the buyer. Yet רב just described how the owner gets his things back.

keyTerms.meaning: A burglar who breaks in by digging a tunnel
He acquired them with his blood

steps.confusionAlert: 'He acquired them with his blood' does not mean he paid anything. It means that because his life was at risk when he broke in, the law treats the stolen items as his.

phrases.english: And did Rav really say this?
But didn't Rav say: one who came in through a tunnel,
phrases.notes: This is a burglar who digs into a house. The Torah allows the homeowner to kill him (שמות 22:1).

What is the reason? He acquired them with his blood!
phrases.notes: His life was on the line when he broke in, so he becomes the owner of what he took.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב's case definition in step 45, the גמרא challenges רב from another ruling of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's position that the owner recovers his items from the buyer in the משנה's case (steps 39 and 45).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a burglar acquires what he steals, the stolen items belong to the thieves, and the owner should have no claim against someone who bought from them.

steps.title: Only a real burglar risked his life; guests did not
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a thief acquires the items applies only to a בא במחתרת, who put his life at risk from the start. These guests never risked being killed, so they do not acquire the items.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule, that he acquires them, applies to a burglar who came in through a tunnel, since from the start he put his life at risk of being killed. But these guests, since they did not put their lives at risk of being killed, do not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two rulings of רב deal with different kinds of thieves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Acquiring with blood' only works for someone the homeowner was allowed to kill, meaning a real burglar who broke in. The guests came in legitimately as guests, so their lives were never at risk. They therefore never acquire the items, and the owner can take them back.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to... (introduces a limit)
He put himself at risk of being killed

steps.whatToRemember: A thief 'acquires with his blood' only if he could have been killed, like a real burglar. Guests who steal never had that risk, so the stolen items still belong to the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the burglar's exemption is not a general rule for all thieves. It depends on the risk to his life, which is exactly what the guests lacked.

but these,
phrases.notes: He means the guests from our case, who stayed in the house and stole.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מְסַרוּ נַפְשַׁיְיהוּ לִקְטָלָא – לָא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 46.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a burglar versus guests.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every thief who took items through a tunnel acquires them with his blood, including the guests.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a thief who risked being killed, like a real burglar, acquires. Guests did not risk their lives, so they do not acquire, and the owner takes back his items.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule to an owner who usually sells his vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the rule we learned applies only to a בעל הבית who usually sells his vessels. He begins to contrast this with a בעל הבית who does not usually sell them, and the sentence continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We only learned this rule about a homeowner who is used to selling his vessels. But a homeowner who is not used to selling his vessels...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is narrowing the rule we have been discussing to one kind of owner. He is setting up a contrast with a second kind of owner, and the ruling for that owner comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא spoke about every owner the same way. רבא splits owners into two groups: one who sometimes sells his own vessels, and one who never does. The rule we learned fits the first group. The second group will be treated differently in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: We only learned this about (a phrase that limits a rule to a certain case)
Homeowner; the owner of the house and the vessels
Who is used to selling; who usually sells

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא already gave the ruling for the owner who does not sell his vessels. The sentence stops in the middle. That ruling comes in the next part.

phrases.english: Rava said:
We learned this only

but a homeowner
who is not used to selling his vessels –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case was fully defined and the challenge from רב's own ruling was answered, רבא adds a new limit based on what kind of owner is involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule we learned applies to a בעל הבית who usually sells his vessels. A בעל הבית who does not usually sell them is treated differently, as the next part explains.
